about.title: A full stack developer with a product mindset
about.lead: I'm Valentina Moreno, a Full-Stack Developer with 6+ years of experience building web applications, from user interfaces and experiences to APIs, business logic, and service integrations.
paragraphs: I move comfortably between front-end and back-end: I define component architecture, model API contracts and make sure the experience holds up when data grows or fails.
I'm curious, collaborative and focused on measurable outcomes. I document, I review code and I make sure knowledge stays with the team rather than in one person's head.
Beyond code I care about accessibility, perceived performance and interfaces that make a hard number understandable at first glance.

items.title: Cripto — real-time market dashboard
items.summary: An application that consumes market APIs to classify and visualise the current value of currencies and cryptocurrencies, with rankings, price changes and continuously updating data.
items.challenge: Presenting constantly changing price series without making the interface unreadable or losing performance on modest devices.
items.solution: I built a dashboard with ranking cards, currency formatting and explicit loading and error states, backed by data fetching decoupled from the presentation layer.
highlights: Separation between data fetching and rendering so the API provider can change without touching the UI.
Currency and large-number formatting with Intl, avoiding precision mistakes when displaying figures.
Loading skeletons and empty states instead of blank screens while data is in flight.

items.title: Rick & Morty — explorer with dynamic routes
items.summary: An application consuming a public API to display details of characters, locations and episodes, using dynamic routing and efficient state management.
items.challenge: Sustaining deep navigation and combined filters without reloading the app or duplicating requests.
items.solution: I implemented per-entity dynamic routes, result caching and a state layer that avoids re-fetching data already visited.
highlights: Dynamic routes with parameters so any detail page can be shared as a direct link.
Client-side caching to cut repeated requests and improve perceived speed.
Detail components reused across different entities.

items.title: To-Do — task management with persistence
items.summary: A task list built with React Hooks and browser local storage, with real-time updates and persistence across sessions.
items.challenge: Keeping state in sync with local storage without breaking the experience when the user reloads or closes the tab.
items.solution: I created Hook-driven state synchronised with localStorage, supporting create, complete and delete operations.
highlights: Derived state and explicit synchronisation with localStorage on every mutation.
Small, focused components that are easy to test in isolation.
Keyboard-operable interface for adding and completing tasks.

items.title: Bad Jokes — playful API integration
items.summary: An application consuming a jokes API to browse and share them interactively, with careful loading and error states.
items.challenge: Delivering a snappy experience on top of an external API that can be slow or fail.
items.solution: I implemented the integration with explicit error handling, clear interaction controls and a lightweight interface centred on the main action.
highlights: Visible error handling for the user instead of silent failures.
A minimal interface that prioritises the main action on a single screen.
Reusable custom styles without heavy dependencies.
